name: Jeju Island
region: Jeju, island south of the peninsula
tagline: A volcanic island of lava tubes, a snow-capped crater, tangerine groves, black-rock coasts and white-sand coves, an hour by air from Seoul.
highlight: Sunrise from the crater rim of Seongsan Ilchulbong, with the sea turning gold below.
shortDescription: South Korea's volcanic island, with Hallasan mountain, the Seongsan Ilchulbong tuff cone, Manjanggul Lava Tube, beaches like Hyeopjae, tangerine farms and the female divers of the haenyeo.
metaDescription: A Jeju Island travel guide: Hallasan hiking, Seongsan Ilchulbong, Manjanggul Lava Tube, Hyeopjae Beach, haenyeo divers, black pork, tangerines, where to stay, how to get around and a three-day plan.
knownFor: Volcanic landscapes, Hallasan, beaches, haenyeo divers, tangerines
budget: US$100–190 per day, mid-range, plus a car
goodFor: Scenery, hiking, road trips, beaches, honeymooners

image.file: File:Hydrangea macrophylla in front of Seongsan Ilchulbong volcano at blue hour in Jeju Island South Korea.jpg
image.alt: Hydrangea flowers in front of the Seongsan Ilchulbong volcanic cone at blue hour

intro: Jeju is a volcanic island about 85 km south of the Korean peninsula, built by eruptions over about two million years. It is dominated by Hallasan, at 1,947 metres the highest mountain in South Korea, and dotted with hundreds of smaller cones called oreum, with a coast of black basalt cliffs, sea caves and pale beaches. The island's volcanic landscape and lava tubes are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Jeju has its own culture. The island's dialect, stone walls, stone grandfather statues called dol hareubang and its haenyeo, female divers who harvest seafood on a single breath, set it apart from the mainland, and the haenyeo tradition is on UNESCO's intangible heritage list. Food is distinctive too, with black pork, abalone, tangerines and hallabong fruit.

Jeju is a classic short Korean holiday, an hour by air from Seoul and Busan, and the busiest air route in the world. It is best with a car, since sights are spread around the coast. Three days covers Seongsan, the lava tube, Hallasan and a beach, and spring and autumn are the best seasons, though the rapeseed flowers of spring and the winter camellias have their own following.

whyVisit.intro: Jeju is Korea's natural showpiece, a scenic island with a culture of its own.

points.title: A volcanic landscape
points.text: Hallasan, craters, lava tubes and basalt cliffs.

points.title: Beaches and coast
points.text: White sand and turquoise water at Hyeopjae.

points.title: Unique culture
points.text: Haenyeo divers, stone walls and local dialect.

points.title: Easy to reach
points.text: About an hour by air from Seoul.

attractionsIntro: Sights are spread around the coast and the volcano, so a car is the best way to link them.

attractions.name: Seongsan Ilchulbong

image.alt: The Seongsan Ilchulbong tuff cone rising from the sea on Jeju Island

attractions.text: A 180-metre tuff cone formed by an undersea eruption, with a grassy crater rim reached by a 20-minute climb. It is famed for sunrise.
attractions.tip: Go for sunrise, or late afternoon.

attractions.name: Hallasan National Park

image.file: File:Wooden staircase along Yeongsil Trail with the mountains of Hallasan Park Jeju Island South Korea.jpg
image.alt: A wooden staircase along the Yeongsil Trail with Hallasan mountains beyond

attractions.text: A dormant volcano with a crater lake at its summit, and trails such as Yeongsil, Eorimok and the long Seongpanak and Gwaneumsa routes.
attractions.tip: Reserve summit trails online, and start early.

attractions.name: Manjanggul Lava Tube

image.alt: The dark interior of Manjanggul Lava Tube on Jeju

attractions.text: One of the world's longest lava tubes, with a section open to walkers, and tall passages, lava columns and a cool temperature.

attractions.name: Hyeopjae Beach

image.alt: The pale sand and turquoise water of Hyeopjae Beach on Jeju

attractions.text: A beach on the west coast with pale sand, clear water and views of Biyangdo island.

attractions.name: Jeju Haenyeo Museum
attractions.text: A museum in the north-east about the female free divers and their culture.
attractions.tip: Combine with a coastal seafood lunch.

attractions.name: Oreum volcanic hills
attractions.text: Small volcanic cones that are easy to climb, with sweeping views, such as Saebyeol Oreum and Yongnuni.

thingsToDoIntro: Jeju is for driving, hiking and slow coastal stops.

thingsToDo.title: Climb Hallasan
thingsToDo.text: Hike Korea's highest peak in one long day.
thingsToDo.tip: Book the trail slot and start at dawn.

thingsToDo.title: Drive the coast
thingsToDo.text: Loop the island road, stopping at beaches and cliffs.
thingsToDo.tip: Rent a car for three days.

thingsToDo.title: Watch a haenyeo dive
thingsToDo.text: See divers work at Seongsan or Hado.

thingsToDo.title: Walk the Olle Trails
thingsToDo.tip: Follow the blue and orange ribbons.

thingsToDo.title: Visit a tangerine farm
thingsToDo.text: Pick fruit in autumn and winter.

foodIntro: Jeju's food is built on black pork, seafood and citrus.

foods.name: Black pork (heukdwaeji)
foods.text: Grilled slabs of Jeju's black pig.

foods.name: Hallabong and tangerines
foods.text: Citrus fruit grown on the island.

foods.name: Grilled cutlassfish
foods.text: A silvery fish from local waters.

foods.name: Green tea and citrus desserts
foods.text: Green tea from the Osulloc fields.

accommodation.intro: Base yourself in Jeju City or Seogwipo, or by a beach.

areas.name: Jeju City
areas.text: The main city on the north coast.

areas.name: Seogwipo
areas.text: A quieter town on the south coast.

areas.name: West coast (Hyeopjae)
areas.text: Pensions and cafés by the sea.

gettingThere.intro: Jeju is reached by air from Seoul, Busan and other cities.

options.text: About one hour from Gimpo, with many flights daily.
Overnight ferries from Mokpo and Wando take several hours.

gettingAround.intro: A car is the best way to see the island.

options.text: The best option. Foreign visitors need an international driving permit.
options.detail: Book ahead and use Kakao Navi or Naver Map.

options.text: Buses connect towns but are slow.

bestTime.headline: April–May and September–October
bestTime.summary: Jeju is milder than the mainland in winter but windy, and it is rainy in summer.

seasons.text: Rapeseed and cherry blossoms in April.
Beach season, but humid, rainy and busy.
Clear, with silver grass on the oreum.
Cool and windy, with snow on Hallasan and winter camellias.

bestTime.avoid: Typhoon days in late summer and autumn.

itinerary.title: Three days on Jeju
itinerary.intro: The east on the first day, the mountain on the second, and the west coast on the third.

tipsIntro: A few tips make Jeju easier.
tips: Rent a car, and get an international driving permit.
Check the weather, since fog and wind can close trails.
Use Naver Map or Kakao Map.
Do not touch or feed wild horses.

faq.q: How many days do you need on Jeju?
faq.a: Three days is good, and four to five allow a slower pace.
It is the easiest way. Buses and taxis work for a few sights.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit?
faq.a: April to May and September to October.

faq.q: Can I hike Hallasan in a day?
faq.a: Yes, it takes about 8 hours return, and requires a reservation for the summit trails.

faq.q: Do I need a visa for Jeju?
faq.a: Jeju has had a visa-free policy for many nationalities. Check current rules.
